query: How can sellers improve Amazon product satisfaction?

per_column.name: sentiment
per_column.rationale: Sentiment (positive/negative) is essentially a proxy for product satisfaction itself, the focus/outcome, not an intervenable treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: mentioned_topics
per_column.rationale: Topics such as product_quality, sizing_fit, shipping_packaging, customer_service, pricing map to actionable levers a seller could change. As drivers of satisfaction they function as candidate intervenable treatments, though here they are extracted from the review text and thus partly mediating the expressed sentiment.

per_column.name: seller_improvement_signal
per_column.rationale: Directly encodes an intervenable action a seller could take (improve quality, clarify sizing, improve shipping, review pricing). This is genuinely settable/decidable and aligns with the what-if framing.

per_column.name: review_length_bucket
per_column.rationale: A mechanical property of the review text; not a common cause of both an intervenable treatment and satisfaction. Does not serve as a confounder.

judge.rationale: The added columns do identify intervenable treatments (seller_improvement_signal is an explicit settable action; mentioned_topics maps to configurable product/service levers), satisfying part (a) of the what-if claim. However, the set completely fails part (b): there is NO confounder among the added columns. A valid what-if design needs common causes of both the treatment (e.g., which improvement is pursued) and the outcome (satisfaction) to be adjusted for — for example product category, price tier, brand reputation, buyer expectations, or reviewer demographics, none of which appear. sentiment restates the outcome, and review_length_bucket is a mechanical text feature (mediator/noise at best, not a confounder). Because no confounders are present, none can be scored as named-or-unnamed, so the interventional counterfactual effect cannot be read off. The columns are reasonable as descriptive/attribution aids but do not realise a proper interventional design.
